---
title: Slurm arrays
description: Submit, throttle, and inspect HTSeq jobs on a Slurm cluster.
---

Slurm submits all samples as one array. Each task reads one generated TSV row,
avoiding shell parsing of paths and sample identifiers.

```bash
htseq-count-cluster run \
  --scheduler slurm \
  --infile samples.csv \
  --gtf genes.gtf \
  --outpath counts \
  --partition short \
  --account my-allocation \
  --memory 4G \
  --time 02:00:00 \
  --max-concurrent 8
```

`--max-concurrent 8` limits concurrent tasks to eight. The CPU count is a
scheduler request; `htseq-count` remains a single-process command.

## Check status once

```bash
htseq-count-cluster status --scheduler slurm 12345678
```

The command queries `squeue`, then `sacct` after the job leaves the queue, and
reports `Queued`, `Running`, `Finished`, `Failed`, or `Unknown` without polling.

## Inspect failures

Logs under the submission's `logs/` directory include job and array-task
identifiers. Use them to diagnose failures; the manifest and `run-array.sh`
record inputs and the task command.
